title: Adaptive page-stitched KV reuse with prefill holdback for decode-latency smoothing
text:
Adaptive page-stitched KV reuse with prefill holdback for decode-latency smoothing

description:
Reduce tail decode latency and KV cache churn by introducing an adaptive page-stitching reuse layer and a configurable prefill holdback that smooths decode wave arrival patterns for paged attention workloads.

background:
We observe repetitive tail latencies during bursts where multiple long-context requests cause aggressive KV eviction and subsequent prefill storms. Existing LRU-like reclamation causes oscillation: pages reloaded just after eviction, causing decode stalls and kernel swapping. Prior tickets explored eviction heuristics and prefill scheduling, but customers still hit 95th/99th percentile latency spikes for mixed short/long workloads.

goals:
1) Reduce 95th/99th token decode latency under mixed-workload bursts by ~20-30%. 2) Reduce redundant page reloads (same-token ranges) by at least 30% for multi-tenant shards. 3) Introduce a low-overhead coordination mechanism compatible with Dedicated and Hosted modes.

proposal_summary:
Add a lightweight page-stitching metadata layer that records recent contiguous token spans (stitches) across paged KV slots and exposes a reusable handle. Use a probabilistic soft-reservation (holdback) that prevents immediate eviction for recently stitched spans. Pair this with a prefill holdback: newly requested prefills are delayed by a small, adaptive window when a decode wave pattern indicates a cascade risk. The runtime will prioritize kernel affinity for stitched pages to avoid kernel hopping.

design_notes:
- Stitching: maintain compact Bloom-filter-like fingerprints per page-span to detect likely contiguous reuses without full metadata blowup.
- Soft-reservation: per-tenant token-credit that decays over time; credits granted when a stitch is observed.
- Holdback window: computed from moving avg of inter-arrival times of prefill requests per shard; min 2ms, max 50ms.
- Kernel affinity: extend kernel selection table to prefer kernels that already host pages referenced by incoming decode wave to avoid memory migration.
- Metrics: new counters for stitch-hits, holdback-delayed-prefill, avoided-evictions, kernel-affinity-misses.

implementation_plan:
1) Prototype stitch metadata structures and API (Phase A). 2) Integrate smart soft-reservation accounting into allocator (Phase B). 3) Implement adaptive holdback timer in prefill scheduler and tie to inter-arrival estimator (Phase C). 4) Kernel affinity hints: pass page handles through kernel selector; lightweight weighting heuristic (Phase D). 5) Canary on dedicated pool, monitor metrics, iterate (Phase E).

tasks:
A1: Implement compact span fingerprint store + unit tests
A2: Bench microbench for false-positive rate and memory overhead
B1: Add soft-reservation accounting to KV allocator
B2: Simulate multi-tenant contest scenarios to tune decay parameters
C1: Implement adaptive holdback in prefill scheduler
C2: Hook into runtime tracing to record holdback decisions
D1: Extend kernel selector to accept page-stitch hints
D2: Update kernel selection benchmarks to measure hopping reduction
E1: Canary rollout on dedicated small pool and collect 95/99pct latencies
E2: Dashboard: stitch metrics + eviction-reload charts

acceptance_criteria:
- 95th token decode latency reduced by >=20% in synthetic mixed short/long burst workloads.
- Stitch-hit ratio >= 30% in representative traces.
- No >5% increase in average memory overhead for stitch metadata.
- No regression on single-tenant throughput microbenchmarks.
- Observatory dashboard shows holdback events and corresponding latency smoothing.

risks_mitigations:
- FP in fingerprinting may hold pages unnecessarily -> mitigate via decay and bounded soft-reservation budget.
- Holdback delaying necessary prefills may increase median latency -> adaptive window with low floor and integrated feedback: abort holdback if queue backlog rises.
- Kernel affinity weighting could worsen load imbalance -> cap affinity weight and fallback to global balancer.

progress_updates:
2026-02-22: Spike complete for compact span fingerprint; memory overhead ~0.8% in microbench (Asha)
2026-03-02: Soft-reservation accounting sketch reviewed by Miguel + Priya; recommended decay constant adjustments
2026-03-08: Holdback scheduler initial implementation landed in feature branch (PR #4823); integration tests failing under extreme backlog scenarios
2026-03-12: Introduced backlog bypass to abort holdback when backlog > threshold; tests stabilized
2026-03-14: Canary scheduled for small dedicated pool starting 2026-03-16 (Miguel)

review_feedback:
Priya Rao: Ensure stitch metadata is eviction-friendly; prefer forward-only ring buffer and avoid mutex hot paths.
Samir Ahmed: Add metric for 'holdback-abort' to reason about when adaptive window is bypassing.
Design: Consider UX exposure for tuning holdback window per-customer on Dedicated plans.

qa_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprint false-positive and metadata GC.
- Integration tests with injected multi-tenant burst traces.
- Load test on dedicated canary pool with synthetic traffic mix.
- End-to-end regression run against legacy eviction policy for throughput and p95/p99.

deployment_notes:
Feature gated via runtime flag 'page_stitch_reuse_v1' and prefill_holdback_ms. Default OFF for Hosted in initial rollout; ON for selected Dedicated tenants. Toggleable via Console rollout control.

postmortem_criteria:
If 95/99 latencies worsen for canary >10% for 30m, roll back flag and capture trace for root-cause analysis.
